facts.value: Biomedical engineering (BME) or medical engineering is the application of engineering principles and design concepts to medicine and biology for healthcare applications (e.g., diagnostic or therapeutic purposes). BME also integrates the logical sciences to advance health care treatment.

Prominent biomedical engineering applications include the development of biocompatible prostheses, diagnostic and therapeutic medical devices, imaging technologies such as MRI and EKG/ECG, regenerative tissue growth, and the development of pharmaceutical drugs including biopharmaceuticals.

Bioinformatics is an interdisciplinary field that develops methods and software tools for understanding biological data, combining computer science, statistics, mathematics, and engineering to analyze and interpret biological data.

Biomechanics is the study of the structure and function of the mechanical aspects of biological systems, at any level from whole organisms to cells and cell organelles, using the methods of mechanics.

A biomaterial is any matter, surface, or construct that interacts with living systems. The study of biomaterials is called biomaterials science or biomaterials engineering, encompassing medicine, biology, chemistry, tissue engineering, and materials science.

Biomedical optics combines physics, engineering, and biology to study the interaction of biological tissue and light, with applications in optical imaging, microscopy, ophthalmoscopy, spectroscopy, and therapy.
Tissue engineering is a major segment of biotechnology, aimed at creating artificial organs such as kidneys and livers for patients needing organ transplants.
Genetic engineering involves the direct manipulation of an organism's genes using modern tools to alter the structure and characteristics of target genes.
Neural engineering uses engineering techniques to understand, repair, replace, or enhance neural systems, including the development of cognitive neural prosthetics.
Pharmaceutical engineering is an interdisciplinary science that focuses on drug engineering, novel drug delivery, and pharmaceutical technology.
A medical device is intended for use in the diagnosis of disease or other conditions, in the cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease.
Imaging technologies are essential to medical diagnosis and include fluoroscopy, MRI, nuclear medicine, PET, X-rays, and ultrasound.
